claims.evidence: Three SILAC mixtures were deposited, one per RAW zip, each 16 fraction runs, each searched separately in MaxQuant (three SEARCH zips). One source per (cell population, mixture). IMPORTANT: the zip labels and the MaxQuant search labels are swapped for experiments 2 and 3: the 16 embedded acquisition names in 3rdexperiment-MS.zip (I 8_2_1..I 8_2_16, acquired 2017-09-08/09 in folder 20170906HHF_SILAC) are exactly the Raw files of the MaxQuant "2nd experiment" search, and those in 2ndexperiment-MS.zip (I 8_1, I 8_4, I 8_5, I 8_8, I 8_10, I 8_11, I 8_12, I 8_14, I 8_15, I 8_16 from 2017-09-06/08 plus re-runs I 8_2_2, I 8_2_3, I 8_2_6, I 8_2_7, I 8_2_9, I 8_2_13 from 2017-09-13/14 in folder 20170913HHF) are exactly the Raw files of the MaxQuant "3rd experiment" search. 1stexperiment-MS.zip = 20160818_hhf-I_1..16 = MaxQuant "1st experiment". Source names follow the deposited RAW zips (what a user downloads).

claims.value: SILAC light = parental HCT116; SILAC heavy = highly invasive subline HCT116-I8 (all three mixtures)
claims.evidence: PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol: "HCT116-I8 and HCT116 cells were cultured ... either light media (Arg0, Lys0) or heavy media (Arg10, Lys8) ... The lysates of heavy-labeled HCT116-I8 and light-labeled HCT116 cells were mixed with equal amounts". Every deposited file is named H-HCT116-I8-<n> (H = heavy HCT116-I8). Data check: the paper (abstract) reports upregulation of Cdc42BPA in HCT116-I8; deposited log2 H/L normalized of CDC42BPA (Q5VT25) = +0.87 / +1.05 / +1.25 in the 1st / 2nd / 3rd MaxQuant searches -> heavy = HCT116-I8. Searches correlate positively (Pearson log2 H/L 0.73-0.77, n 3388-3579), so no label swap between mixtures. Conflict recorded: CDH1 log2 H/L is +0.45..+0.53 although the abstract reports decreased E-cadherin (western blot) in I8 cells; the explicit label statement, the file names and the paper's headline protein outrank this.

claims.value: highly invasive subline HCT116-I8 / parental HCT116
claims.evidence: PRIDE projectDescription / abstract: "Eight rounds of selection of cancer cells invading through matrigel-coated chamber was performed to obtain highly invasive colon cancer sublines HCT116-I8 and RKO-I8"; "HCT116-I8 ... cells showed significantly stronger invasive potential ... compared with parental cells". Custom use of the TERMS.tsv phenotype column (EFO:0000651, free text allowed) outside its clinical-metadata template (spec Extending Templates) to carry the subline identity, because HCT116-I8 has no Cellosaurus or ontology record.

PRIDE names the deposits 1st/2nd/3rd experiment; each is a separately fractionated (16 fractions) and separately searched SILAC mixture acquired on different dates (2016-08-18/20; 2017-09-06/08 + 2017-09-13/14 re-runs; 2017-09-08/09). Peptide content differs between mixtures (same-fraction Jaccard 0.37-0.58, i.e. not identical injections). Whether each mixture came from an independently grown culture pair is not stated (paper Methods not accessible): treated as independent labelling experiments.

Both populations are HCT116 (parental) or derived from it (HCT116-I8, selected from HCT116 by eight rounds of Matrigel invasion). Cellosaurus has no entry for HCT116-I8 (searches q=HCT116-I8, id:"HCT 116-I8", hi:CVCL_0291 AND (sy:*I8* OR id:*I8*), hi:CVCL_0291 AND invasive: no hit; log cello_search_I8.txt), so the parental term is used (precedent PXD005246). EFO:0002824 label "HCT116" (Cellosaurus DR EFO_0002824), not obsolete.
Cellosaurus AC CVCL_0291, ID "HCT 116" (SY HCT116). Parental line of HCT116-I8 (no derivative entry).
PRIDE organisms NEWT:9606; Cellosaurus OX NCBI_TaxID=9606; OLS NCBITaxon:9606 Homo sapiens.
Cellosaurus CVCL_0291 "Derived from site: In situ; Colon; UBERON=UBERON_0001155"; OLS UBERON:0001155 label colon.
Cellosaurus DI NCIt C4910 Colon carcinoma; OLS MONDO:0002032 colon carcinoma (not obsolete). PRIDE diseases DOID:219 colon cancer (broader). Both populations are tumour-derived, so no normal arm.
Cultured cell lines (SILAC culture in RPMI 1640).
Cellosaurus CC "Population: Caucasian."; OLS HANCESTRO:0005 European ancestry.
Cellosaurus AG 48Y, SX Male; donor age >= 20Y -> EFO:0001272 adult (batch rule 9).
Both populations derive from the single HCT 116 donor (HCT116-I8 is selected from parental HCT116).
PRIDE protocol: "SILAC RPMI 1640 media (Thermo Fisher Scientific), supplemented with 10% dialytic fetal bovine serum"; OLS NCIT:C178973 Roswell Park Memorial Institute 1640 Medium, not obsolete.

claims.value: H-HCT116-I8-<n>.wiff (member basename inside its RAW zip; identical basenames recur in the three zips)
claims.evidence: The deposit exposes the vendor raw files only inside 1st/2nd/3rdexperiment-MS.zip; each zip holds H-HCT116-I8-1..16.wiff (+ .scan / .wiff.scan companion). The same 16 basenames occur in all three zips (different files, CRCs differ), so comment[data file] repeats across mixtures; the assay name carries the zip prefix to keep runs distinct (precedent PXD009311 names the .wiff member inside a zip).

sdrf-tools build gives the file stem; the deterministic post-build script postbuild.py prefixes the zip stem (from the source name suffix exp1/2/3) because the three zips use identical member names. Nothing else is edited.

claims.value: 1-16 per mixture; exp1/exp3: = file number; exp2: assigned from peptide content
claims.evidence: exp1 (1stexperiment-MS.zip, 20160818_hhf-I_<n>) and exp3 (3rdexperiment-MS.zip, I 8_2_<n>) runs were acquired in number order ~1 h 44 min apart, and run n of each overlaps best with run n of the other (Jaccard 0.37-0.47). exp2 (2ndexperiment-MS.zip): for 8 of 16 files the embedded name number does not match the peptide content: best-matching fraction (mean Jaccard to fraction n of the other two mixtures) vs value at the name number: I 8_2_3 -> 6 (0.515 vs 0.003), I 8_2_6 -> 7 (0.520 vs 0.175), I 8_2_7 -> 9 (0.504 vs 0.024), I 8_2_9 -> 13 (0.451 vs 0.011), I 8_2_13 -> 3 (0.476 vs 0.024), I 8_14 -> 16 (0.420 vs 0.024), I 8_15 -> 14 (0.451 vs 0.053), I 8_16 -> 15 (0.445 vs 0.077); second-best <= 0.19 everywhere. The assigned set is a permutation of 1-16. The six re-runs (2017-09-13/14) fill exactly the six acquisition-time gaps of the 2017-09-06/08 series (fractions 2,3,6,7,9,13), so the mislabel is a permutation within that set. Fraction identifiers therefore follow content: deposited files 1,2,13,4,5,3,6,8,7,10,11,12,9,15,16,14 = fractions 1-16. The fractionation method itself is not documented.
One injection per (mixture, fraction) in the deposit and in each MaxQuant search; superseded first injections of the exp2 re-run fractions were not deposited.

Every .wiff (SCIEX Analyst TF 1.6 data file) carries "Mass Spectrometer:TripleTOF 5600 ... Component Name: Hybrid Quadrupole-TOF LC/MS/MS Mass Spectrometer, Component ID: TripleTOF 5600+, Manufacturer: AB Sciex Instruments" (checked fully in 1stexperiment-MS H-HCT116-I8-1.wiff); MaxQuant msmsScans Mass analyzer = TOF. PRIDE instruments field (MS:1000449 LTQ Orbitrap) and the protocol sentence about an LTQ-Orbitrap are contradicted by the vendor format and the raw header (an LTQ Orbitrap cannot write .wiff); rejected.
MaxQuant processed the runs as standard DDA (MS/MS of selected precursors; msmsScans Type ISO/MULTI/PEAK, Fragmentation CID); acquisition method SILAC_8ul_90min.dam / SILAC_6ul_90min.dam.
QqTOF (TripleTOF 5600+) fragments in the q2 collision cell = beam-type CID; MaxQuant reports Fragmentation "CID". Campaign precedent PXD004880 (TripleTOF 5600) uses MS:1000422.
MaxQuant msmsScans.txt column Mass analyzer = TOF; QqTOF instrument.

MaxQuant summary.txt Enzyme "Trypsin", Enzyme mode "Specific", max 2 missed cleavages, in all three searches, giving 72,527-76,559 MS/MS-identified evidences and 12-18 % identified MS/MS per run; a non-tryptic digest would not identify at this rate in a specific trypsin search. The PRIDE protocol says only "Protein digestion and MS analysis were performed as described previously"; the digestion enzyme is not named in the accessible record (reconcile finding refuted in validation.txt).

MaxQuant 1.5.2.8 parameters.txt/summary.txt do not record the precursor (first/main search) tolerance and no mqpar.xml was deposited.
16 fractions per mixture, but the method is only referenced ("as described previously") and the paper Methods were not accessible.

limitations: Paper (J Proteome Res 2018, doi:10.1021/acs.jproteome.7b00550) is closed access; only the abstract and the PRIDE protocol texts were available. Biological-replicate independence, fractionation method, digestion details and reduction/alkylation reagents are therefore not documented.

Deposited zip labels vs MaxQuant search labels are swapped for experiments 2 and 3 (2ndexperiment-MS.zip = MaxQuant "3rd experiment"; 3rdexperiment-MS.zip = MaxQuant "2nd experiment"), established from embedded .wiff acquisition names; source names follow the zips.

exp2 fraction identifiers for 8 files are assigned from peptide-content similarity, not from file names (the embedded acquisition names of those files are permuted relative to content); see the fraction-identifier claim.

comment[data file] basenames H-HCT116-I8-1..16.wiff repeat in the three RAW zips; a pipeline must take each file from the zip named by the assay-name prefix. Raw files are only available inside the zips (with .scan companions).

PRIDE instrument field and protocol (LTQ Orbitrap, 350-1500 m/z, 35K resolution, "middle versus light" ratio) describe a different instrument/experiment and are contradicted by the .wiff headers; no MS1 scan range was annotated.

CDH1 (E-cadherin) log2 H/L is +0.45..+0.53 in the deposited searches while the abstract reports decreased E-cadherin by western blot in I8 cells; channel map kept from the explicit PRIDE label statement, file names (H-HCT116-I8) and CDC42BPA (+0.87..+1.25).
Precursor mass tolerance not recorded by MaxQuant 1.5.2.8 -> not available; convert-openms fails on it (expected).
RKO-I8 (also named in the abstract) has no runs in this deposit; scope = HCT116-I8 vs HCT116 only.
Independent review not run here: hand-off to an external reviewer (REVIEW_PENDING_EXTERNAL).
